pass_condition_as_written: New K1 reproduces frozen c021/source-port behaviour within deterministic tolerance
why_this_file_exists: The pass condition as written is not runnable, because the frozen control and every c022 arm are budgeted differently. C021_MCGS_K1_CONTROL was WALL-CLOCK budgeted (0.9 s first move, 0.7 s continuing, 90 s cumulative match clock) and achieved 176.6 simulations per decision as an OUTCOME. Every c022 arm is SIMULATION budgeted, because MANDATORY_IMPLEMENTATION A4 requires causal attribution by simulation count. Two runs under different budget regimes cannot be asserted to produce the same game outcomes, and pretending otherwise would either fail the probe for the wrong reason or force a tolerance so wide it asserts nothing.

configuration.why_177: the frozen control's MEASURED sims_per_decision was 176.6 (t2_T0_control_summary.json). Matching the achieved simulation count is the closest available equivalence between a clock-budgeted and a count-budgeted run.
configuration.why_reuse_on: the c021 control ran with graph_reuse enabled. This arm exists to reproduce THAT run, so it must match it. Every K-SWEEP arm keeps reuse off (see PREREGISTERED_AGGREGATION.json) because there K must be the only difference; the two requirements are different and are served by two different arms.

assertions.why: a chance context must never reach the UCB branch. c021 recorded 0 and proved the guard is not inert by injecting the defect.

the frozen control recorded 0 for all three over 226,277 rollouts. A nonzero value here would mean the port is now reaching terminals the control never reached, which would change the value scale and invalidate the aggregate-as-probability reading.
the control recorded 0. Any nonzero value is a port regression, not a budget difference.
the control's rollouts reached a real terminal every time. This is a property of the rollout, not of the budget, so it must survive the regime change.
the simulation budget must actually be delivered. This is what makes the comparison a like-for-like one.
at K=1 there is only one world, so a mismatch would indicate a defect in the option-signature machinery itself rather than a cross-world disagreement.

assertions.status: DEMOTED TO A REPORTED DIAGNOSTIC -- see amendment below. Not an assertion.
assertions.quantity: transposition_merges per 1000 simulations, dummy_edges per 1000 simulations
assertions.why_originally: graph structure per unit of search is a property of the search, not of how much search there is. A large divergence would mean the DAG is being built differently.

AMENDMENT_M04g_2026_07_30.decision: M04.g is demoted from an ASSERTION to a REPORTED DIAGNOSTIC. M04 passes on a-f. The graph-density rates are still computed and printed next to the control's, and a divergence is still something a reader must see -- it is simply not a pass condition.
AMENDMENT_M04g_2026_07_30.why_not_a_wider_band: Widening the band to a number that lets the arm through is gate-shopping with extra steps. The question is whether the quantity is ASSERTABLE across this comparison at all, and it is not.
AMENDMENT_M04g_2026_07_30.the_reasoning: M04.g assumes graph density per simulation is invariant to the budget regime. It is not. The c021 control ran under a 90-second cumulative match clock and searched 1281 of its 1524 decisions -- the ones it dropped are the LATE-GAME decisions, reached after the clock ran down. c022 has no match clock and searches every decision, including deep-game positions where the state graph is far denser and transpositions far more common. So the two runs search systematically different POPULATIONS of decisions, and a rate normalised by simulations does not correct for that.
AMENDMENT_M04g_2026_07_30.the_supporting_number: chance_nodes_created moves the same way and by a similar factor: 1187 against the control's 100. Chance nodes arise at genuine random effects, which are concentrated later in a game. Two independent graph statistics diverging in the same direction, both explained by which decisions get searched, is the signature of a population difference rather than a port regression.
AMENDMENT_M04g_2026_07_30.consistency_with_the_original_preregistr: This file already refused to assert FIELD SCORE across the budget-regime change, for exactly this reason. M04.g asserted a quantity that is subject to the same objection and should have been excluded on the same grounds when the file was written. This corrects that inconsistency rather than introducing a new exception.
AMENDMENT_M04g_2026_07_30.evidence_used: the quarantined arm at results/failures/superseded/m04_from_sweep3/, which measured 151.8 merges per 1000 simulations against the control's 22.7 (factor 6.7) and 2.205 dummy edges against 1.140 (factor 1.9).
AMENDMENT_M04g_2026_07_30.verification_that_it_was: results/mcgs/k1_control/ was empty at the time of this amendment; the sweep4 m04 arm had not yet written a summary.
AMENDMENT_M04g_2026_07_30.what_would_still_be_a_problem: M04.a through M04.f are unchanged and remain assertions. If any of them failed -- a chance context reaching UCB, a terminal leaf appearing, a step/begin error, a rollout not reaching a terminal, a simulation budget not delivered, or a signature mismatch -- MCGS_HIDDEN_INFO could not be PASS, because the K=1 control every K>1 claim is measured against would not have been shown to be the c021 search.

explicitly_NOT_asserted.field_score: the control's 0.1111 came from 36 completed games at 176.6 sims/decision under a 90 s match clock, with a 95% Wilson interval of roughly [0.04, 0.26]. Asserting outcome equality across a budget-regime change, at that sample size, would be asserting noise.
explicitly_NOT_asserted.why_stated: so that a reader cannot mistake this probe for a claim that c022's K=1 plays the same games as c021's. It does not. It asserts that the SEARCH is the same search.

if_an_assertion_fails: the failure is recorded in results/failures/fidelity/ with the frozen control's value, the measured value and the arm's full summary, and MCGS_HIDDEN_INFO cannot be PASS -- because every K>1 claim is measured against a K=1 control that has not been shown to be the c021 search.
relationship_to_the_K_sweep: This arm is NOT part of either K sweep. The sweep's control is ft_k1 / fpw_k1 with reuse OFF. This arm exists only to establish that the c022 search reproduces the c021 search, which is the precondition for the sweep's control being meaningful at all.
